landers.name: Generic CLPS-class lander (parametric)
landers.note: Parametric class similar to Nova-C / Blue Ghost; edit freely.

landers.name: Nova-C class (Intuitive Machines)
landers.note: ≈1,908 kg launch mass, VR900 (≈900 lbf ≈ 4 kN) LOX/methane main engine; Isp not published — ~340 s assumed for a vacuum methalox engine. IM-2: PDI at 13 km, ≈14.5 min before touchdown.

landers.name: Blue Ghost class (Firefly) — Mission 1 as flown
landers.note: Published M1 figures: launch mass 1,517 kg, dry 469 kg, ten NASA payloads ≈94 kg (TO 19D) → ≈954 kg MMH/MON-3; payload capacity 155 kg (NSSDCA) trades against propellant at the same launch mass. LEROS 4-ET main engine (>1 kN, Isp ≈320 s) + 8 Spectre RCS (1.6 kN total) fire together for braking (≈2.6 kN); terminal descent on pulsed RCS. M1: LOI burn 4 min 15 s, DOI ≈T−63 min, 9-min PDI burn 1,700 → 40 m/s from ≈20 km. The budget closes with only ≈10 kg to spare — as tight as the real mission.

landers.name: Apollo Lunar Module (descent stage)
landers.note: DPS 45 kN throttleable 10–60 % + full; landed mass ≈7.3–8.2 t.

landers.name: Vikram class (ISRO Chandrayaan-3)
landers.note: 4 × 800 N throttleable engines; 1,752 kg lander module incl. rover.

launchVehicles.name: SpaceX Falcon 9
launchVehicles.note: Approx. TLI capacity with booster recovery.

transfers.name: Direct transfer (~4.5 days)
transfers.note: CLPS-style direct injection with mid-course corrections.

transfers.name: Fast transfer (~3 days, Apollo-like)
transfers.note: Higher arrival speed → larger LOI burn.

transfers.name: Earth phasing loops + transfer (~30 days)
transfers.note: Blue Ghost / Chandrayaan style: several Earth-orbit raising burns before TLI.

transfers.name: Delivered to lunar orbit by a carrier/propulsion module (~5 days)
transfers.note: Apollo CSM / Chandrayaan-3 propulsion-module style: the lander only performs DOI + powered descent.

transfers.name: Low-energy (weak stability boundary, ~100 days)
transfers.note: Hakuto-R / CAPSTONE style; smallest LOI burn, longest cruise.
